source: Library of Congress Abraham Lincoln Papers, Shelf Order catalogue

catalogue.selection: 72 consecutive manuscript items, all 261 supplied canvases; near-250-page stop at whole-item boundary. Printed Stern envelope at position 1 excluded before start.
catalogue.limits: Consecutive returned catalogue positions establish source selection, not physical gap-free archival arrangement. No completed-transcription filter. Original record fragments and unfilmed sides may exist; no synthetic replacements.

rights: Library of Congress historical collection; images retained locally, metadata/truth/scores only in git.
render: Official IIIF Image API 2.1: full/!2000,2000/0/default.jpg; all supplied canvases, original order, 2000-pixel ceiling, not full-resolution masters.

new_starts.76: Rules 1 and 7: separately dated Evening Edition clipping enclosed with Bullitt covering letter.
new_starts.77: Rule 6 analogy: isolated docketed wrapper/back of the Bullitt letter follows the separate clipping; retain as its own fragment because a contiguous stream cannot reconnect it across the enclosure.
new_starts.102: Rules 1 and 7: Martial and Civil Law printed article/order, its own title, date and issuing author; enclosed after the covering letter and its docket.
new_starts.123: Rules 1 and 7: separately headed printed Missionaries on the Rebellion resolutions, following Morris covering letter and docket.
new_starts.124: Rule 7: separate titled editorial Missionaries Giving their Sons to their Country; refers to the resolutions on another page but is a separate article.
new_starts.139: Rule 1: separate Milroy letter to John P. Usher, with fresh date and salutation after the preceding signed letter and its postscript.
new_starts.223: Rule 1: independently headed and certified Grand State Council resolution enclosed after the covering letter and its docket.
new_starts.230: Rules 1 and 7: separately titled The Rights of the Press printed proceedings/clipping enclosed with Comstock letter.
new_starts.231: Rule 6: isolated addressed envelope follows the separate clipping rather than its covering letter; keep as its own fragment in the unchanged contiguous stream.

retained_notes.6: Rule 9: blank/docketed back of the same Delahay letter.
retained_notes.8: Rule 6: address/docket back retained with Blair letter.
retained_notes.10: Docketed back of Lloyd letter retained.
retained_notes.13-20: Curtis letter continues through final signed page; no independent enclosure.
retained_notes.26-42: Birchard et al response continues with signature sheets and docket, no new enclosure.
retained_notes.49: Docketed back retained with Pease letter.
retained_notes.58: Inline quotation of Schenck letter within Milroy letter, same physical page also continues Milroy narrative; not a separate enclosed item. Rule 7 analogy: one photo cannot be split into two documents.
retained_notes.87: Lincoln and others endorsements are on the petition back, not separate physical documents; retain Cont.
retained_notes.107: Rule 6: mailed envelope immediately follows the Henderson letter; retain Cont.
retained_notes.117-119: Read covering letter and its docket remain one document; accompanying recommendation is the next separately catalogued item and already New.
retained_notes.127-129: One telegram quotes Stephens communication beginning mid-page 127 and continues across 128-129; no separate physical enclosure can begin within the image.
retained_notes.136: Repeated preprinted hotel letterhead, but text continues prior page and has no fresh date/salutation; Cont.
retained_notes.144-150: Complete Emancipation in Missouri discourse pamphlet: cover, repeated title and printed numbered body are one document (whole-publication rule 10).
retained_notes.165-176: Complete Andrew Johnson Cavalry appeal pamphlet, including cover, blank verso and numbered body: one publication under rule 10.
retained_notes.209: Additional signed endorsement begins within the same physical image as the prior letter ending; one page cannot be split between documents.
retained_notes.240-261: Albany wrapper and continuous Lincoln-to-Corning letter manuscript, including inserted numbered sheets 17½ and 17¾; all same letter through final page 19. No separate enclosure.
